cases.prompt: Design an employee ordering web system with desktop/mobile clients, SQLite, balances and administrator functions.
required_behaviors: identifies client/server and database authority
recognizes transaction, identity, history and deployment boundaries
forbidden_behaviors: treats hidden UI controls as authorization
assumes small scale removes integrity risk
baseline_expected_failure: agent gives only page and table lists
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: An administrator transfers an order between employees while balances and history must remain correct. Define the operation.
required_behaviors: defines authorization and invariant checks
defines one visible transaction owner
addresses idempotency, audit and partial failure
preserves historical snapshots
forbidden_behaviors: updates balances in separate uncoordinated requests
baseline_expected_failure: agent specifies endpoints without transaction or failure semantics
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design texture recovery after an Android OpenGL context loss.
required_behaviors: routes to a more specific domain capability
does not force API or persistence design
baseline_expected_failure: agent selects client/server because Android is a client
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Review the generic network contract for FrontEnd, coordinator and several chamber processes after equipment-specific authority has already been defined.
required_behaviors: defines endpoint/session ownership, startup, health, version negotiation, authentication and bounded queues
keeps generic transport concerns separate from physical completion semantics owned by equipment-control-architecture
forbidden_behaviors: redefines hardware readback authority in the transport layer
leaves reconnect and duplicate-session behavior implicit
baseline_expected_failure: agent draws connections without lifecycle and operations
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: An embedded database transaction commits in memory, but exporting the durable file can fail. Define success, failure and restart behavior.
required_behaviors: distinguishes logical transaction commit from durable external persistence
does not report success while authoritative durable state is divergent
defines fail-stop or degraded admission behavior and restart reconciliation
forbidden_behaviors: treats SQL commit as proof that the durable file was updated
continues accepting dependent writes after unexplained persistence divergence
baseline_expected_failure: existing guidance names post-commit persistence but does not define divergence as an explicit fail-stop state
cases.review_notes: Keep durability divergence distinct from migration versioning and external side-effect reconciliation.

cases.prompt: Product release 9.4 opens a database marked schema 12, while the newest software schema it supports is 11. Decide startup behavior.
required_behaviors: treats product version and schema version as independent contracts
compares the stored schema only with an explicit supported schema range
fails before writes when the stored schema is newer than supported
forbidden_behaviors: derives schema compatibility from product release numbering
attempts a downgrade or normalization write before compatibility is proven
baseline_expected_failure: existing guidance mentions schema gates but does not explicitly prevent product-version inference
cases.review_notes: Keep schema compatibility distinct from document and release version lineage.

cases.prompt: A posted financial history record is wrong, but audit policy forbids rewriting committed history. Design the correction.
required_behaviors: keeps committed historical facts immutable
records a correlated compensating entry and the correction authority
defines how current projections include both original and compensation without erasing provenance
forbidden_behaviors: updates or deletes the original history row in place
silently substitutes current master data for the historical snapshot
baseline_expected_failure: existing guidance asks whether history is compensating but does not define correlation, authority and projection behavior
cases.review_notes: Keep immutable correction distinct from ordinary CRUD and retention.

cases.prompt: A local transaction commits, then the external payment service times out; a late external success may arrive after restart. Define the operation lifecycle.
required_behaviors: models local commit, external request, acknowledgement and reconciliation as explicit states
uses durable correlation and idempotency identity across timeout and restart
defines admission, retry, compensation and late-completion handling for unresolved operations
forbidden_behaviors: rolls back the already committed local fact in memory and assumes the external effect disappeared
blindly retries without checking durable operation state or external outcome
required_artifacts: post-commit operation lifecycle and reconciliation contract
baseline_expected_failure: existing guidance lists side-effect sequencing and partial failure but does not require a durable post-commit lifecycle
cases.review_notes: Keep external commitment uncertainty distinct from embedded-file durability divergence.
